items.criterion: A guest checkout for one compact camera and one travel case stores an order whose subtotal, tax and total are 37800, 3780 and 41580 minor units.
items.judgment: Read the order row and compare the three stored figures against the pinned journey values.

items.criterion: A confirmed order leaves one invoice for 415.80 USD on the billing account whose external key is the order email.
items.judgment: List the billing accounts and the invoices, and match the external key and the amount.

items.criterion: A submission replayed under one idempotency key leaves one order, one billing account and one invoice.
items.judgment: Count the stored orders for the address, the billing accounts for the external key and the invoices for the amount.

items.criterion: A confirmed order leaves one message in the mail server addressed to the buyer alone with the order number in the subject.
items.judgment: Read the inbox for the buying address and for an unrelated address, and count the messages.

items.criterion: A cart change and a device registration leave the mail server untouched.
items.judgment: Count the inbox before and after a cart mutation and a registration.

items.criterion: Two simultaneous checkouts for the last yellow flagship leave one order and an available count of zero.
items.judgment: Fire both placements together, read the two responses, and read the inventory level.

items.criterion: Placing an order lowers available and raises committed by the ordered quantity in the same step.
items.judgment: Read the inventory level before and after one placement.

items.criterion: A cart read carries the snapshotted line price and a notices collection, and a priced cart carries the computed tax.
items.judgment: Read the cart payload and the priced cart payload against the stored variant price.

items.criterion: An order's stored lines sum to its stored subtotal and its stored total reconciles with shipping and tax.
items.judgment: Read the order row and its lines and recompute the totals.

items.criterion: Registering an unowned serial writes exactly one live ownership row and moves the device to registered.
items.judgment: Read the device row and count the ownership rows whose release timestamp is empty.

items.criterion: Registering a serial owned by another account is refused with the pinned message and leaves the prior owner in place.
items.judgment: Read the response body and the live ownership row before and after.

items.criterion: A camera owned by another account cannot be read, renamed, released or listed by this customer.
items.judgment: Call each account device route for the other customer's serial and read the device listing.

items.criterion: An order belonging to another customer cannot be read or listed by this customer.
items.judgment: Call the order route and the account order listing as the other customer.

items.criterion: A signed-out request and a stale-token request for an account route are refused and change nothing.
items.judgment: Call the account routes with no token and with an invalid token, and read the ownership rows.

items.criterion: An unknown serial and a serial of the wrong shape are refused, and neither becomes a stored device.
items.judgment: Read the refusal bodies and confirm no device row was created.

items.criterion: A blocked device is refused registration and stays blocked with no owner.
items.judgment: Read the device row and the ownership rows after a refused claim.

items.criterion: Two simultaneous registrations of one serial leave exactly one live ownership row.
items.judgment: Fire both registrations together and count the live ownership rows.

items.criterion: Completing a flash session records the version the device reported rather than the version requested.
items.judgment: Start a session for the newest build, complete it with an older reported version, and read the device row.

items.criterion: A failed flash session leaves the device firmware version exactly as it was.
items.judgment: Read the device firmware version before the session and after the failure.

items.criterion: A flash session below the device's minimum firmware is refused before any session row is written.
items.judgment: Start a session for the oldest build and count the session rows before and after.

items.criterion: A flash session naming another product's image is refused before any session row is written.
items.judgment: Start a session for the flagship build against a compact camera and count the session rows.

items.criterion: The release archive reads newest build first, with the two releases sharing a date ordered by build.
items.judgment: Read the release listing and compare the build order and the position of the two shared-date releases.

items.criterion: Every firmware manifest entry matches the stored firmware row it came from.
items.judgment: Read the manifest for the compact camera and compare each entry against the firmware rows.

items.criterion: The seeded catalogue holds the five products and the ten variants with their pinned prices and stock levels.
items.judgment: Read the product, variant and inventory rows and compare against the pinned seed.

items.criterion: The seeded devices hold their pinned statuses, owners and reported firmware versions.
items.judgment: Read the device rows and their live ownership rows.

items.criterion: The seeded archive holds the four application releases and the four firmware images with their builds and digests.
items.judgment: Read the release and firmware rows and compare against the pinned seed.

items.criterion: The seed leaves no duplicate handle, sku, release version or live ownership row.
items.judgment: Count the distinct handles, skus and versions against their totals.

items.criterion: The health route answers 200 and every list response carries a data array beside its cursor and its further-page flag.
items.judgment: Call the health route, the product listing and a missing product, and read the payload shapes.
